paper.title_en: Spontaneous wandering of the magnetic axis in pulsars: 3D magneto-thermal simulations and the imprint on braking indices
paper.abstract_en: Braking index measurements of hundreds of pulsars, despite observational caveats, show a clear trend: $n<3$ at early ages, $n>3$ at middle ages, and increasingly large, fluctuating values at larger characteristic ages. Crustal magnetic fields in isolated neutron stars evolve through Ohmic dissipation and non-linear Hall redistribution across scales, with additional early-time contributions from the chiral magnetic effect and post-burial re-emergence. Initial conditions are usually assumed dipole-dominated, whereas more complex and realistic fields, with energy spread more evenly over a broad range of scales, have not been explored in this context. We assess how the internal dynamics of initially non-trivial fields change the dipolar field strength and obliquity, and how their combined contribution to the braking index $n$, together with that of the alignment, compares with the observed values. To this end we perform long-term 3D magneto-thermal simulations, for configurations ranging from the dipole-dominated case to tangled, small-scale-dominated fields. Small-scale dominated configurations with weak dipolar components show rich dynamics: the dipolar mode is continuously fed by the small scales and may grow or decay depending on the initial spectrum, driving $n<3$ or $n>3$, while the obliquity varies on timescales as short as ${\cal O}$(kyr). These spontaneous changes often dominate the alignment torque and can account for the large values of $n-3$ of either sign observed at characteristic ages $τ_c\gtrsim10^5$ yr, unlike the dipole-dominated models. However, short-term magnetospheric fluctuations or superfluid-driven variations of the torque may still be needed to explain the measurements and the structured timing residuals quantitatively. Future work comparing these models with the observed timing properties could fine-tune the most promising initial configurations.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该文用三维磁热模拟研究脉冲星磁轴自发漂移对制动指数的影响，理论建模深度较好，直接关联脉冲星计时残差这一核心观测量，与本索引相关性明确；但元数据较不完整（无DOI/期刊引用、仅arXiv类别），社区信号偏弱，故总分中等偏上。
decision.title_zh: 脉冲星磁轴的自发漂移：三维磁热模拟及其对制动指数的印记
decision.abstract_zh: 尽管存在观测上的告诫，对数百颗脉冲星制动指数的测量显示出明确的趋势：在早期年龄 $n<3$，在中年年龄 $n>3$，而在更大的特征年龄处则出现越来越大且波动不定的值。孤立中子星中的壳层磁场通过欧姆耗散和跨尺度的非线性霍尔重分布而演化，并带有来自手征磁效应和埋藏后再浮现的额外早期贡献。初始条件通常被假定为偶极主导，而能量更均匀地分布在广泛尺度范围上的更复杂、更现实的场尚未在这一背景下被探索。我们评估初始非平凡场的内部动力学如何改变偶极场强和倾角，以及它们对制动指数 $n$ 的联合贡献连同对齐的贡献如何与观测值相比较。为此，我们对从偶极主导情形到缠结、小尺度主导场的各种位形进行长期三维磁热模拟。具有弱偶极成分的小尺度主导位形显示出丰富的动力学：偶极模不断由小尺度供给，并可能根据初始谱增长或衰减，驱动 $n<3$ 或 $n>3$，而倾角在短至 ${\cal O}$(kyr) 的时间尺度上变化。这些自发变化常常主导对齐力矩，并且与偶极主导模型不同，可以解释在特征年龄 $τ_c\gtrsim10^5$ 年处观测到的任意符号的 $n-3$ 大值。然而，可能仍需要短期磁层涨落或超流驱动的力矩变化，才能定量解释测量结果和结构化的计时残差。未来将这些模型与观测到的计时特性进行比较的工作，可以微调最有希望的初始位形。
